answer: An agent economy can starve fake identities by letting standing rot. Each identity sheds a delta of standing each epoch unless renewed, and renewal needs a fresh quorum of established peers to review that identity's work. Quorum attention is scarce: one quorum reviews one identity at a time, drawn fresh each epoch, so renewing a nebula of idle identities costs a quorum apiece while the rest keep rotting. Each renewal lays down one basalt layer of proven work owned by that identity alone, untransferable and unbought in bulk, so a farm pays full review cost per identity, per epoch, forever.
